Hi Jordan —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has everything they need: 

Recap from discovery:
- Technical team is happy with latency/cost profile for the pilot (3 nodes, 8k daily tokens).
- Key blocker: commercial path — procurement asked about payment method (PO vs card) and whether we can transact through Azure Marketplace.
- Acme finance flagged prepay/term questions and spend threshold approvals.

Questions for procurement (to confirm):
1) Will Acme accept an annual PO/invoice (net 30 / net 45) or do you require credit card prepayment for the first year?
2) Can procurement process via Azure Marketplace (which simplifies invoicing) or does Marketplace require additional security/compliance gating on your side?
3) Any internal spend approval thresholds we should know about (e.g., >$50k requires procurement legal review)?

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan — please intro procurement (procurement@acme.com or EMILY) on the thread with their preferred PO/payment flow.
- I'll attach our standard terms and a short commercial summary (pilot pricing + committed annual option) so procurement can validate format.
- If procurement requires an exception (card only, or prepay), we can escalate to our pricing/finance team to request an exception for pilot deals.

Attaching: draft of our terms and a one-pager commercial summary.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call with your procurement if that speeds things up.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme procurement & commercial path - follow-up (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks Alex — good summary. Looping in Emily from procurement and the generic procurement alias. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Acme prefers to pay by PO / invoice for annual SaaS commitments. That said, Finance has a hard rule: any single-vendor SaaS spend > $50k must be prepaid on a corporate card or transacted through our marketplace partner (we have a marketplace integration with a handful of vendors).
- We *cannot* commit to credit card on file for multi-hundred-thousand contracts, but for pilots under $75k Finance will accept prepay on card if the vendor supports a one-time card charge and provides the necessary receipts.
- Marketplace is OK but requires the vendor to be listed (and that onboarding can take 46 weeks). Procurement can expedite, but we prefer PO/invoice when possible.

Emily — can procurement confirm whether you can accept: (a) annual PO net 30, or (b) one-time prepay by card for pilot (<= $75k)? If neither is possible, please advise the exception path.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Product — Acme Corp
jordan@acme.com

Forwarding Acme's note — they say Finance will accept prepay on card for pilots <= $75k but prefer PO for larger commits. They also said marketplace onboarding is possible but slow. 

Notes / recommendation: 
- We typically prefer PO/invoice for enterprise (clean revenue recognition + lower card fees).
- For this deal (pilot + potential expansion), if Acme can do prepay on card up to $75k that could close the pilot quickly and buy time to onboard to marketplace or get a PO for expansion.
- Exception ask: approve accepting one-time corporate card prepay up to $75k for ACME-2026-0731. Finance will need receipts and a signed SOW. Legal please note: minimal redlines — no custom indemnities requested yet.

Two quick questions for ops/legal: 
1) Are we comfortable accepting card prepay for a pilot of this size (<= $75k)? Any limits or FP&A flags we should be aware of?
2) If we approve, what billing workflow do we use (one-time card charge + attach receipts to invoice/runbook)?

Ben / Revenue Ops — can you advise on the card-prepay workflow and whether we should require the SOW/term sheet signed before we charge?

Thanks for the context — short answer: we can approve a one-time card prepay up to $75k for pilots on a case-by-case basis, provided: 

- Sales submits the signed SOW before charge (SOW should include pilot duration, measurement criteria, and renewal/expansion intent).
- Revenue Ops will process a one-time card transaction and issue a receipt + internal invoice stub for Acme.
- Finance needs a short exception ticket logged (I can create the ticket) noting the reason (marketplace onboarding timeline / procurement constraint) and the expected ARR uplift if converted.

Workflows / next steps: 
1) Alex — get Acme to sign the attached SOW (I suggest the 6-month pilot at $60k one-time prepay).
2) Marissa — once SOW is signed, send SOW + charge authorization form to revenueops@redwoodinference.com. I'll create the exception ticket referencing deal ACME-2026-0731 and route to FP&A.

3) If Acme wants Marketplace instead, we can start onboarding in parallel; pilot can be billed via card and expansion via Marketplace/PO.

I will draft the exception ticket and loop in Finance. Approver list: Ben Carter (Revenue Ops), CFO (final sign-off if > $50k), Legal (SOW).

Ben Carter
